BEGIN PROMPT

PLAN TEASER 00 | THE LIGHT CHOOSES
DURATION 20 SECONDS | HORIZONTAL 16:9
EIGHT DISTINCT SHOTS WITH HARD CUTS

CHARACTER REFERENCES
{{CHAR_LEAD_PRISON_GUARD}}
{{CHAR_PRISON_GUARD_TWO}}
{{CHAR_PRISON_GUARD_THREE}}
{{CHAR_SELECTED_PRISONER}}
{{CHAR_CELL_PRISONERS}}

LOCATION REFERENCES
{{LOC_CROWDED_HOLDING_CELL}}
{{LOC_CELL_SERVICE_CORRIDOR}}

PROP REFERENCES
{{PROP_BARRED_CELL_DOOR}}
{{PROP_CELL_LOCK}}
{{PROP_GUARD_FLASHLIGHT}}

Create a 20-second live-action cinematic prison teaser using eight separate camera setups.

The camera is physically trapped near frightened prisoners. Fear is visible in their attempts to retreat, protect themselves and escape the moving light.

The lead guard conducts a silent, humiliating selection game using his pointing finger and flashlight. His irregular gestures and deliberate pauses suggest a childish choosing game.

IDENTITY AND MASK CONTINUITY

All captives are adult men.

Preserve the exact referenced identities, costumes, proportions and handmade masks. Each mask remains rigidly attached, with stable features and eye openings.

The selected prisoner is an anonymous captive.

Perform fear through visible eyes, recoiling shoulders, trembling hands, interrupted breathing and bodies pressing against one another.

START STATE AND BLOCKING

All prisoners stand upright in a tightly packed group inside the cell. Their feet remain on the same continuous floor. They have only a few centimeters of space to retreat.

The barred cell door is closed and locked.

Viewed from the corridor looking into the cell:
The selected prisoner stands just right of center, half a meter behind the bars.
His neighbor stands immediately to his left.
Other prisoners crowd behind and beside them.

The lead guard stands centrally outside the bars, facing inward.

Guard Two stands behind him to screen right, beside the door lock.
Guard Three stands behind him to screen left.

The lead guard holds a flashlight in his LEFT HAND.
He points with his RIGHT INDEX FINGER.
Preserve these hand assignments throughout.

Guard Three holds a second flashlight aimed low toward the prisoners' hands and torsos.

LIGHTING

The general room lights are switched off.

Almost the entire corridor and cell are black.

One tightly restricted hard overhead spotlight illuminates a small area around the lead guard's shoulders and upper body. Its spill barely touches the nearest bars. The surrounding architecture remains largely invisible.

The prisoners are revealed primarily by moving flashlights.

Use narrow, hard-edged pools of illumination across masks, fingers and clothing. Faces emerge briefly from darkness, then disappear when the light moves away.

The lead guard's flashlight is the dominant moving source.
Guard Three's weaker beam stays lower and intermittently reveals tense hands and crowded bodies.

Keep the air clear. Show flashlight illumination through its contact with surfaces.

Expose for the illuminated masks and hands. Maintain deep surrounding darkness when the flashlight leaves a subject.

Location references provide geometry and materials. Replace their existing illumination with this dark lighting arrangement.

SHOT T00-01 | 0s–2s | 2 SECONDS
INSIDE THE CROWD

24mm handheld at chest height inside the cell, facing the bars.

Begin between two prisoners' shoulders. Bodies occupy both foreground edges, leaving a narrow view of the lead guard outside.

A flashlight sweeps across the nearest prisoner's mask. He jerks his head aside and presses backward, bumping the camera operator.

The camera makes a short involuntary sideways correction.

Through the gap, briefly reveal the lead guard beneath the restricted overhead light and the two guards behind him.

Sound: close uneven breathing, fabric friction and a shoe scraping stone.

Hard cut.

SHOT T00-02 | 2s–4s | 2 SECONDS
THE GUARD PREPARES THE GAME

35mm low handheld from inside the cell, close to the bars, looking upward toward the lead guard.

His mask occupies upper center. His left-hand flashlight sits lower in frame, aimed through the bars.

He raises his right index finger above the flashlight.

He shifts his weight with casual confidence while the camera recoils slightly from the approaching light.

His companions remain fragmented silhouettes behind him.

At approximately 3 seconds, he begins the silent choosing gesture, pointing toward one prisoner and pausing.

Sound: a guard's boot adjusting against the floor, glove friction and a captive's caught breath.

Hard cut.

SHOT T00-03 | 4s–7s | 3 SECONDS
LIGHT MOVES BETWEEN PRISONERS

35mm over the lead guard's right shoulder from the corridor, looking into the cell.

His pointing right hand occupies the near foreground. His left-hand flashlight remains visible lower and farther left.

His finger and flashlight move between the same targets together:
a prisoner near the left bars;
a sudden jump several people right;
then a return toward the center.

Use an irregular rhythm: a quick change, a longer hold, then two shorter shifts.

Each illuminated prisoner reacts differently.

One raises a forearm toward his eyes.
Another twists sideways behind a neighboring shoulder.
Another tries to step backward and meets the packed bodies behind him.

The camera makes short lateral adjustments to follow the targets. Keep the pointing hand and illuminated person spatially connected.

Sound: overlapping uneven breaths, restrained nonverbal gasps, feet dragging and clothing tightening.

Hard cut on a change of flashlight direction.

SHOT T00-04 | 7s–9s | 2 SECONDS
A BODY TRIES TO HIDE

28mm handheld inside the cell, beside the selected prisoner's left shoulder, looking diagonally across the front row toward the bars.

The flashlight lands on the selected prisoner.

He ducks his chin and tries to withdraw behind his neighbor. The crowd stops his retreat. His free hand braces against the neighboring man's upper arm.

The neighbor also recoils, compressing both bodies into the camera's space.

The operator takes a short uneven step, briefly loses the eyes behind a moving shoulder, then recovers them.

Sound: a sharp inhalation, compressed fabric and bodies making dull contact.

Hard cut.

SHOT T00-05 | 9s–12s | 3 SECONDS
THE GUARD PROLONGS THE GAME

50mm tight oblique view from the corridor along the barred frontage.

The lead guard occupies the left foreground in profile, facing screen right toward the cell. The prisoners occupy the right background through the bars.

His left wrist rotates the flashlight between captives. His right index finger marks the same targets with deliberately uneven pauses.

He holds on one frightened man, studies the reaction, then skips him.

Behind the lead guard, Guard Three inclines his masked head with quiet amusement. His own flashlight stays pointed lower.

The camera moves physically sideways by half a step, revealing the lead guard's finger and its current target in the same composition.

Sound: quiet glove movement, a small boot scrape and frightened breathing from inside the cell.

Hard cut.

SHOT T00-06 | 12s–17s | 5 SECONDS
A MOMENT OF FALSE RELIEF

50mm tight handheld from the corridor, close to a gap between the bars, framing the selected prisoner's mask, upper chest and gripping hand.

The lead guard's fingertip is softly visible near the lower edge, aligned with the prisoner.

12–14 seconds:
The flashlight settles directly on the prisoner's mask and upper chest.
He freezes mid-breath.
His fingers tighten around the fabric at his sternum.
The camera makes a hesitant physical move closer, disturbed by small operator tremors.

14–15.5 seconds:
The flashlight and pointing finger move away together toward his neighbor.
The selected prisoner's mask falls back into near-darkness.
His shoulders release slightly and one breath escapes.

15.5–17 seconds:
Hold on his uncertain relief.
His eyes continue tracking the guard's hand.
His fingers begin to loosen, but his body remains pressed against the prisoners behind him.

Keep this passage continuous so the tightening and release belong to the same body.

Sound: a held breath becoming a fragile exhalation, fingers releasing fabric and a faint nonverbal sob nearby.

Hard cut at 17 seconds.

SHOT T00-07 | 17s–19s | 2 SECONDS
THE CHOICE IS FINAL

32mm handheld from inside the cell, immediately behind the selected prisoner's right shoulder, looking outward.

His shoulder and rear mask edge occupy the right foreground.

The lead guard faces him beyond the bars at center frame.

At the beginning of this shot, his right index finger and left-hand flashlight return decisively to the selected prisoner and stop.

The prisoner flinches and draws inward. His shoulder bumps the person behind him. The operator jolts backward a few centimeters, then recovers the guard in frame.

The lead guard tilts his masked head slightly while keeping his finger and light fixed.

Guard Two steps toward the lock and reaches it.
Guard Three remains behind, relaxed.

Sound: a sudden involuntary gasp, fabric rubbing against another body and one approaching guard's footstep.

Hard cut.

SHOT T00-08 | 19s–20s | 1 SECOND
THE LOCK

85mm tight handheld detail from the corridor side.

Guard Two's hand is already operating the lock.

Spill from Guard Three's flashlight catches the hand and metal mechanism.

The locking bolt withdraws. The door remains closed.

A dry metal click.

CUT TO BLACK immediately.

END STATE AND EDIT

The selected prisoner remains inside the cell.
The lead guard keeps the flashlight and pointing finger fixed on him.
The lock has released.
The door remains closed at the final visible moment.

End with black and silence.

CAMERA EXECUTION

Deliver eight distinct shots, cutting at:
2s, 4s, 7s, 9s, 12s, 17s and 19s.

Every cut changes physical camera position, viewpoint or lens.

Use handheld movement motivated by crowd pressure, recoiling bodies, hurried reframing and the operator's unstable breathing.

Change framing through physical camera movement and hard cuts.

Allow brief focus slips and foreground obstruction, followed by recovery on the essential gesture or reaction.

Keep the relationship between the pointing finger, flashlight target and prisoner's reaction readable.

SOUND DESIGN — ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS ONLY

Build the soundtrack entirely from sounds physically present in the scene:

uneven captive breathing;
interrupted inhalations;
restrained nonverbal gasps and sobs;
fabric pulled tight by gripping hands;
shoes scraping stone;
small body contacts within the crowd;
gloves shifting around the flashlight;
a guard approaching the lock;
the final metallic release.

Use natural short reflections from the stone corridor. Keep breathing intimate in the close prisoner shots and more distant in the corridor views.

All characters remain verbally silent. The prison loudspeakers remain silent.

The lock click is the final sound. Cut immediately to absolute silence with the black frame.

NO SPEECH.
NO COUNTING VOICE.
NO ANNOUNCEMENT.
NO NARRATION.
NO MUSIC.

END PROMPT

Established requirements for this subject:
- No human appears without a mask. Every person on screen, including nobles, gift-bearers, servants and background figures, wears a mask. A figure who is not a named character takes one of the masked caste looks in REF-001, Civilization Caste Board. Never show a bare human face.
